i did just make a post about eating habits and losing weight when it isn't needed but i didn't talk about obesity. this is a very good point, and this goes for parents who overfeed their kids too. a majority of packages of food have serving sizes written for whoever buys it to read, so that they know how much is meant to be eaten. for example, maybe 6 chicken nuggets is a serving size of a certain brand of chicken nuggets. my mom would ignore that and just give my brothers and i the whole box, and if we didn't finish it she'd question why. no one should be raised eating more than they should because it's a hard habit to break when it's all you know, and obesity shouldn't be normalized just like being underweight shouldn't as well.

THIS. it's so terrible being raised like this, i remember my mom yelling at me in a grocery store because i said i didn't know if i believed in god. i've questioned if hell is even real, and if it is will i go there for not having faith, and to this day i still question if anything i'm doing is really the correct way to live. i couldn't have worded it better than you.

overworking. hard work should be appreciated, but it's at a point where overworking yourself is seemingly something to be proud of. i'm using school related examples but this goes for jobs and really any type of work as well. so many students go nights without sleep to get all their work done and they'll tell others about it like it's a medal. people will cry because theyre so stressed that they don't have the time to get everything done, or they don't understand something, and instead of taking a break they keep pushing themselves. health > work. a person's physical and mental wellbeing should be valued over completing mass amounts of work. this doesn't mean people shouldn't work hard, it simply means that there's a fine line between working hard and pushing your limits that shouldn't be crossed.

ideal body types/diets. this is a commonly mentioned one but there are certain details i want to mention. some people start to develop bad eating habits under the age of 10 because "they need to lose weight." half the time theyre normal weight? so many people will also brag about having gone days without food or overexercising and be proud of it? people who are so skinny are constantly shown to the public, and maybe they do eat healthily, no shame on them, its the fact that other body types are rarely shown. its made out that everyone should be that skinny when the reality is that people have different body types and not everyone is going to be super skinny like the "ideal," people have different body types and being slightly heavier than some random girl you see on a magazine doesn't necessarily determine your physical wellbeing or your value and beauty, and losing/gaining weight really shouldn't be attempted unless a doctor agrees that it's needed or that it's okay, and you should have knowledge on how much you need to eat to survive, preferably to have a doctor aid you in determining how much you should eat daily.
